name: Stan Cullis
scopeNote: Manager profile of Stan Cullis, one counted spell: Wolverhampton Wanderers, June 1948 (appointment, Wikipedia: 'In June 1948') to September 1964 (sacked, Wikipedia: 'surprisingly sacked in September 1964'). Day-level dates are not in the pages read. Three league titles (1953-54, 1957-58, 1958-59) and two FA Cup wins (1949, 1960) per the Wolves hall-of-fame summary and the Wikipedia season table. Style: the evidence supports direct, long-passing football with pace down the wings (Mullen, Hancocks) and high tempo, which Cullis himself called 'scientific kick-and-rush football' in All For the Wolves (1960). 'Kick and rush' is the critics' label that Cullis accepted; the Football Times piece also ties the approach to Charles Reep's direct-play theories. Marking (zonal or man) is not documented in the pages read.

spellsCounted.reason: Three league titles, two FA Cup wins and the direct, winger-led style the 'kick and rush' label is attached to.

statedView.quote: Cullis accepts that critics may call Wolves "scientific kick-and-rush football."
Those tactics demand that Wolves play at a tempo which is beyond the capacity of the other side.
I tell my players that they must train until it hurts because it makes them better players on Saturday.
The primary duty of a team is to entertain the public and, for entertainment, the people of Wolverhampton demand first of all...
